svg.title: eFuse controller with an adopter shadow file (proposal)
svg.desc: Proposed change to the eFuse controller for SMC adopter fuses, based on the existing controller and interface shim figure. A second efuse_shadow_regs instance holds the adopter shadow file. It sits behind the same functional and JTAG AXI-Lite multiplexer, address decode, AXI-Lite to APB bridge and APB demultiplexer as the harness shadow file, so the JTAG lifecycle filter in the wrapper governs it too. The address decode routes the adopter window, which sits in smc_external, to the interface path, and the APB demultiplexer gains an adopter target. The adopter instance takes its region locks from ADOPTER_LOCKS in the harness shadow file, issues its sense command through the command multiplexer after the harness sense, and exports smc_adopter_shadow_regs_o. efuse_guard checks program and read targets in the adopter region against the region rules. Green outlines mark new logic, present in the SMC only; numbered markers refer to the impact notes at the bottom.
svg.text: New for adopter fuses, SMC only
Impact of placing the adopter shadow file behind the JTAG mux
JTAG lifecycle filter, unchanged: adopter fuses get the same policy as all fuses. PROD, RMA_SiP or an integrity error blocks JTAG; other states allow it.
Func/JTAG mux: both ports share one APB bridge, so a write to ADOPTER_LOCKS completes before the next adopter-window access from either port.
Address decode: the interface range gains the adopter window, which sits in smc_external and is not contiguous with the MAP and CTRL windows.
APB demux: a fifth target widens the select enum in efuse_pkg from 2 to 3 bits for SMC and SEP; the SEP answers the adopter target with SLVERR.
Adopter instance: the offset is the address minus the window base, so the base needs no alignment. Locked regions read 0xBADCAB1E without SLVERR.
Command mux: stays in sense mode until both instances finish, so fuse_sense_done_o and the SMC reset release wait for the adopter region.
efuse_guard: choose harness or adopter rules from the full bit address; today the byte address wraps at 1 KB and would check adopter targets against harness locks.
